# **GIST Cleaning – Employee Handbook**

## **Residential Cleaning Technician**

*Welcome\! This handbook is designed to help you understand how we work, what we value, and what you can expect as part of the GIST Cleaning team. Thank you for choosing employment with us\!*

---

## **1\. Welcome to GIST Cleaning**

***gist** (jĭst) (n): the main or essential part of a matter.*

The GIST in GIST Cleaning stands for "Getting Into Stuff Together". It may sound sentimental, but it encapsulates our approach, in both acronym and definition: we approach clients’ needs collaboratively to distill the essence of what we can provide for their lives, their homes, or their businesses.

GIST Cleaning is a small, residential-only cleaning, organization and consultancy business built on trust, reliability, and care. Our clients invite us into their homes and places of business, and that trust is something we take very seriously.

As a team member, you are not just cleaning - you are helping create calm, comfort, and safety for real people. We aim to treat our clients *and* our employees with respect, transparency, and humanity.

---

## **2\. Job Duties for Your Position**

### Residential Cleaning Technician

From the usual spit-n'-shine to that bathroom no one talks about, and everything in between, we provide our customers with service they can rely on and a clean home they can be satisfied with. We perform regular upkeep cleaning, tidying, deep cleaning projects, and move-in/move-out cleaning. 

Job duties for each of our available customer packages include, but are not exclusively limited to, the following: 

**Basic Cleaning Package**

* Floor care: sweeping, vacuuming, mopping, everyday messes and staining.  
* Hard surfaces: dusting, sanitizing wipe-down, wood surface care.   
* Furniture: surface cleaning, vacuuming, everyday messes, light upholstery care.  
* Bathrooms: everyday upkeep, including toilets and baths/showers.  
* Basic miscellany: windows, taking out trash, sweeping off steps/porches, cobweb removal, etc.   
* Deep scrubbing: lime/hard water/gunk, kitchen grease buildup, children's wall graffiti, etc.  
* Upon request:  
  * Low-use/low-visibility surfaces: walls, baseboards, decorative shelves, cabinet shelves, etc.  
  * Pet messes: changing litter boxes, cleaning and deodorizing everyday or chronic "potty areas".  
  * High-detail miscellany: dusting window blinds, trophy shelves, sanitizing movie cases, etc.

**Add-Ons**  
These add-on duties are listed on our website, and can be added to basic cleaning services at client request. You will be informed if these duties are requested by any client. 

* **Tidying**: Includes pick-up of dishes, toys, clothes, everyday pet chaos, movies, books, papers, and other clutter. (Also includes labelled put-away bins upon client request; these will be charged for and provided for you by GIST Cleaning management.)  
* **Washing**: Includes washing dishes and/or laundry to client specifications and preferences.  
* **Pet Poop Cleanup**. Charged per occurrence, and adequate pickup supplies must be provided by client. *If you have an issue that makes you unable/unwilling to provide this add-on, please consult with management.* 

**"White Glove" and Move-In/Move-Out Cleaning**

* Any necessary tasks from *Basic Cleaning Package* above, plus:  
* Cleaning inside and under major appliances; ovens, refrigerators, washers & dryers, etc.  
* Scrubbing walls, cabinets, shelves and baseboards.   
* Dusting & vacuuming uncommon areas (heaters and air vents, ceiling fan blades, etc.)  
* Minor mold or mildew elimination.

---

## **3\. Supplies and Transportation**

While it is often industry standard for residential cleaning companies to make their employees purchase their own supplies, and the cost of transportation is often uncompensated, we like to do things differently. Despite being a small business, we make sure we can afford to keep our employees making a living and focusing on quality work. 

### Supplies

Your initial cleaning kit will be provided for you by GIST Cleaning. This includes your vacuum, mopping hardware, cleaning chemicals, rags and brushes, razors and scrapers, carrying totes, and any other necessary supplies. We want to set you up for success from the start\!

You will also be supplied with a company debit card. **\$75 per pay period** will be allotted to this account for supply costs, and you may spend the available balance on replenishing your supplies however you see fit. ***You must keep your receipts*** for your supply purchases; these will be given to your GIST Cleaning manager, due at the end of each pay period.

### Transportation

Each pay period, GIST Cleaning will provide you a Visa gift card in the amount of **\$50**. This gift card is to be used to offset gas costs. You will be given a new gift card for the new pay period at the time you turn in your supply receipts.

If your employment with GIST Cleaning is terminated for any reason, all cards given to you, along with any supplies purchased with business funds, must be returned directly to your GIST Cleaning manager.  
---

## **4\. Scheduling & Timeliness**

### Hours

Most employees in the **Residential Cleaning Technician** role begin working **part-time (approximately 20–25 hours per week)**. Hours may vary depending on client demand, scheduling needs, and seasonal changes.

Additional hours, including the opportunity to move toward full-time work, may be offered by mutual agreement but are not guaranteed.

### Scheduling Expectations

* Work schedules are set in advance whenever possible  
* Reliability and punctuality are very important in residential cleaning, as our clients rely on us to maintain the cleanliness of their homes and often arrange their schedules around our services  
* If you are unable to work a scheduled shift, notify your client and your GIST Cleaning manager as soon as possible  
  * There is no penalty for reasonably cancelling a shift, but doing so chronically or without good reason may be grounds for disciplinary action or termination  
  * If you need to cancel a shift, please make every effort to reschedule the client’s cleaning according to their availability

### Timeliness

Each client has an assigned recurring time slot, scheduled according to their preferences. Given the variable nature of cleaning, there is some flexibility allowed regarding your arrival time. 

* Our timeliness policy dictates that you may arrive **up to 15-30 minutes** outside of your client’s scheduled start time.   
* If you are running any later than this, you must reach out directly to your client to let them know and ensure that your late arrival will not interfere with their schedule  
  * If your late arrival will interfere with a client’s schedule, apologize and discuss rescheduling or rearranging cleaning priorities with the client.   
  * There is no penalty for reasonably running late, but doing so chronically or without good reason may be grounds for disciplinary action or termination

---

## **5\. Pay & Timekeeping**

### Pay

Employees are paid hourly and must accurately record all hours worked using the company’s timekeeping system. Our current starting rate for the **Residential Cleaning Technician** position is **\$18/hour**. 

Overtime is paid according to federal and Idaho law for hours worked over 40 in a work week.

### Reviews & Raises

Employees receive a formal performance review at approximately **six (6) months**, with additional reviews every six months thereafter.

Reviews consider:

* Quality of work  
* Reliability and attendance  
* Client feedback  
* Communication and teamwork

Raises are discretionary and based on performance and business needs. *For detailed information on performance reviews and raises, please see your Employment Agreement, section 4\.*

### Paid Time Off

Paid time off is earned at a rate of **1 hour per 25 hours worked.** You may use your PTO for any of the following:

* Hours missing due to sickness or absence  
* Vacation time  
  * Vacation time that is more than 2 consecutive days must be approved by your GIST Manager. Please reach out at least 3 weeks in advance, or your request may not be approved.   
  * You will be responsible for coordinating your absence with your clients. Please ensure your shifts are covered whenever possible; reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager if you require assistance.  

If you choose to terminate employment with GIST Cleaning, you may claim any unused PTO balance on your final paycheck, ***provided you give a minimum of two weeks’ notice*** and work your scheduled shifts until the time of your termination***.*** *For detailed information on this policy, please refer to your Employment Agreement, section 12\.*  

### Timekeeping

* All time worked must be recorded  
* Working off the clock is not permitted  
* Falsifying time records may result in discipline or termination

We use a service called **Gusto** for our payroll and time tracking. You should have received an invitation for onboarding with Gusto; if you have not received this invitation, please reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager. You can log your hours through Gusto on your mobile device, as well as edit logged hours if needed. 

***Only hours worked on location may be logged***; transportation time to and from clients’ homes do not count towards daily hours worked. Gusto uses geofencing capabilities to assure accuracy, ease and liability management for both employees and management; you will be required to turn on Location settings for Gusto in your mobile device for this capability to function.

We ask that you log your hours promptly and accurately, with as few timecard edits as possible. If you do need to edit your timecard, you will be asked to enter a note explaining the reasons for the edit; please be thorough and succinct. Excessive time card edits may be grounds for corrective action. 

---

## **6\. Conduct & Appearance**

Residential cleaning takes place in the homes and personal spaces of our clients, sometimes while they are home. As such, it is of paramount importance that our employees’ conduct be respectful, accountable, and appropriate. 

### Conduct 

We expect all team members to behave professionally and respectfully. This includes:

* Upholding client confidentiality standards (*see your Employment Agreement document, section 8\.*)  
* No theft, dishonesty, or misuse of property  
* Respectful communication with clients and coworkers  
* Following company policies and instructions

**The following behaviors are considered unacceptable, and are grounds for immediate termination:**

* Harassment of any kind  
* Violent or aggressive behavior  
* Sexually and/or romantically inappropriate or forward behavior towards a client or any person in the client’s home  
* Smoking or vaping at work, either interior or exterior.   
  * If you require nicotine, smoke only in your own vehicle or other public spaces while off-site.  
* Being intoxicated while at work. (*See your Employment Agreement document, section 11\.*)  
  * We also acknowledge that, due to our company’s proximity to Washington state borders, that recreational cannabis usage may be a part of some employees’ lives. A positive result for cannabis on a drug test in and of itself is not grounds for immediate termination, but intoxication via substance use of any sort while on shift is still considered unacceptable and is grounds for termination.  

**The following behaviors are not grounds for immediate termination, but may be subject to corrective action:** 

* Excessive use of cellular or mobile devices, including phone conversation, such that it is interfering with quality or timeliness of work or is noted by clients  
* Excessive talkativeness with clients, such that it is interfering with quality or timeliness of work or intruding upon client’s personal time  
* Loud or disruptive behavior (e.g. loud or emotionally intense phone conversations, loud singing or dancing while clients are present)  
* Any other behavior that consistently interferes with quality or timeliness of work, or is noted as concerning or disruptive by clients

***Please be aware:*** in the state of Idaho, it is legal for one party to record another without notice. This means that, at any time, a client may have cameras in their home and is under no legal obligation to inform either you or GIST Cleaning management. This means that appropriate conduct is ***paramount***, whether or not a client is present.

### Appearance

Though cleaning is dirty work, it is also important that we present ourselves with appropriate cleanliness and professionality. This includes:

* Clean, practical clothing suitable for physical work  
* Good personal hygiene  
* Clothing should be respectful and appropriate for entering private home

---

## **7\. Employee Safety, Wellness & Physical Expectations**

### Physical Expectations

Residential cleaning is physically demanding work. Tasks may include bending, kneeling, lifting, standing for extended periods, scrubbing, and using cleaning products. Employees are expected to be able to perform these tasks with minimal difficulty and no anticipated damage to their body.

### Safety Expectations

* Follow all safety and training instructions on all labels, documents and instructional manuals  
* Use gloves or protective equipment when required or advisable  
* Never mix cleaning chemicals  
* Report injuries, accidents, or unsafe conditions immediately

Please inform us if you have any allergies or sensitivities to certain cleaning chemicals, and we will do our best to accommodate you. 

Your safety matters to us. Please speak up if something feels unsafe.

### Wellness

Employee wellness is a top priority for GIST Cleaning, and maintaining a good work-life balance is highly encouraged. If you find yourself ill or unwell and needing to rest and recover, please consider doing so and rescheduling with your client(s) if possible.

Client wellness is also a top priority. We do serve elderly clients, immunocompromised clients, and/or clients with small children. If you are running a fever and/or are confirmed with a contagious illness (e.g. COVID, influenza, norovirus), it is your responsibility to inform both your GIST Cleaning manager and your client(s)  each day you continue to run a fever and/or remain contagious. 

We always prefer to keep contagious illnesses at home, but understand that some employees may be reluctant to lose out on hours. If you wish to work while contagiously ill, you must receive consent from your client(s) for the day before performing your cleaning duties at their home *and* mask for the duration of your shift(s).

---

## **8\. Client Communication**

You will be largely responsible for communicating with your assigned clients regarding their services, as well as check-ins with management. The following is a quick-glance reference at what is included in your communication responsibilities as a **Residential Cleaning Technician**, and what is not. 

### Employee Responsibilities

* Communicating in person with clients regarding cleaning tasks or other job-related matters as needed  
* Messaging clients if you are running late, or need to cancel/reschedule  
* Coordinating any needed scheduling changes with clients  
  * Please inform your GIST Cleaning manager of any scheduling changes as soon as possible following the change.  
* Coordinating time slots with new clients who are assigned to you after their initial intake, according to availability

### Employer Responsibilities 

* Coordinating new client intakes  
* Assigning new clients to employees for scheduling   
* Addressing client complaints, accidents, or other liability issues

---

## **9\. Inclusivity & Understanding Policy**

From our website: 

“*One of GIST's core functional principles is **individual needs.***

*The key word in that sentence is **individual.***  
*​*  
*GIST is queer-friendly, disability-friendly, and mental health-inclusive.*

*GIST is also a no-shame space. We understand that we all have unique circumstances, both external and internal, that affect how we handle our spaces - and the depth or nature of the help we may need to handle them like we want to.*”

Operating by this policy is a cornerstone of our company culture, and is part of why our clients trust us. By signing this document, you are agreeing to operate according to these principles as a member of the GIST Cleaning team. 

---

## **10\. Anti-Discrimination & Harassment Policy**

GIST Cleaning is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment.

Discrimination or harassment based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, or any other protected status will not be tolerated by or from any GIST Cleaning employee, client, or person present in the client’s home while an employee is on shift.

Concerns should be reported to management promptly and will be taken seriously.

---

## **12\. Discipline & Termination**

We aim to address issues with communication and fairness. Depending on the situation, discipline may include verbal warnings, written warnings, or termination.

Because employment is at-will, termination may occur at any time, with or without cause, as allowed by law.

---

## **13\. Questions & Communication**

We encourage open communication. If you have questions about expectations, scheduling, safety, or anything else, please ask.

We believe the best work happens when people feel informed, respected, and supported.

---

## **14\. Acknowledgment**

This handbook may be updated as needed. Employees will be notified of significant changes.

By signing below, the Employee acknowledges that they have read, understand, and agree to the company policies and guidelines outlined in this document. Once signed, this Agreement serves as a legal addendum to the company document entitled *Employment Agreement*, created by Sipes Enterprises, LLC.

  * There is no penalty for reasonably running late, but doing so chronically or without good reason may be grounds for disciplinary action or termination

---

## **5\. Pay & Timekeeping**

### Pay

Employees are paid hourly and must accurately record all hours worked using the company’s timekeeping system. Our current starting rate for the **Residential Cleaning Technician** position is **\$18/hour**. 

Overtime is paid according to federal and Idaho law for hours worked over 40 in a work week.

### Reviews & Raises

Employees receive a formal performance review at approximately **six (6) months**, with additional reviews every six months thereafter.

Reviews consider:

* Quality of work  
* Reliability and attendance  
* Client feedback  
* Communication and teamwork

Raises are discretionary and based on performance and business needs. *For detailed information on performance reviews and raises, please see your Employment Agreement, section 4\.*

### Paid Time Off

Paid time off is earned at a rate of **1 hour per 25 hours worked.** You may use your PTO for any of the following:

* Hours missing due to sickness or absence  
* Vacation time  
  * Vacation time that is more than 2 consecutive days must be approved by your GIST Manager. Please reach out at least 3 weeks in advance, or your request may not be approved.   
  * You will be responsible for coordinating your absence with your clients. Please ensure your shifts are covered whenever possible; reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager if you require assistance.  

If you choose to terminate employment with GIST Cleaning, you may claim any unused PTO balance on your final paycheck, ***provided you give a minimum of two weeks’ notice*** and work your scheduled shifts until the time of your termination***.*** *For detailed information on this policy, please refer to your Employment Agreement, section 12\.*  

### Timekeeping

* All time worked must be recorded  
* Working off the clock is not permitted  
* Falsifying time records may result in discipline or termination

We use a service called **Gusto** for our payroll and time tracking. You should have received an invitation for onboarding with Gusto; if you have not received this invitation, please reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager. You can log your hours through Gusto on your mobile device, as well as edit logged hours if needed. 

***Only hours worked on location may be logged***; transportation time to and from clients’ homes do not count towards daily hours worked. Gusto uses geofencing capabilities to assure accuracy, ease and liability management for both employees and management; you will be required to turn on Location settings for Gusto in your mobile device for this capability to function.

We ask that you log your hours promptly and accurately, with as few timecard edits as possible. If you do need to edit your timecard, you will be asked to enter a note explaining the reasons for the edit; please be thorough and succinct. Excessive time card edits may be grounds for corrective action. 

---

## **6\. Conduct & Appearance**

Residential cleaning takes place in the homes and personal spaces of our clients, sometimes while they are home. As such, it is of paramount importance that our employees’ conduct be respectful, accountable, and appropriate. 

### Conduct 

We expect all team members to behave professionally and respectfully. This includes:

* Upholding client confidentiality standards (*see your Employment Agreement document, section 8\.*)  
* No theft, dishonesty, or misuse of property  
* Respectful communication with clients and coworkers  
* Following company policies and instructions

**The following behaviors are considered unacceptable, and are grounds for immediate termination:**

* Harassment of any kind  
* Violent or aggressive behavior  
* Sexually and/or romantically inappropriate or forward behavior towards a client or any person in the client’s home  
* Smoking or vaping at work, either interior or exterior.   
  * If you require nicotine, smoke only in your own vehicle or other public spaces while off-site.  
* Being intoxicated while at work. (*See your Employment Agreement document, section 11\.*)  
  * We also acknowledge that, due to our company’s proximity to Washington state borders, that recreational cannabis usage may be a part of some employees’ lives. A positive result for cannabis on a drug test in and of itself is not grounds for immediate termination, but intoxication via substance use of any sort while on shift is still considered unacceptable and is grounds for termination.  

**The following behaviors are not grounds for immediate termination, but may be subject to corrective action:** 

* Excessive use of cellular or mobile devices, including phone conversation, such that it is interfering with quality or timeliness of work or is noted by clients  
* Excessive talkativeness with clients, such that it is interfering with quality or timeliness of work or intruding upon client’s personal time  
* Loud or disruptive behavior (e.g. loud or emotionally intense phone conversations, loud singing or dancing while clients are present)  
* Any other behavior that consistently interferes with quality or timeliness of work, or is noted as concerning or disruptive by clients

***Please be aware:*** in the state of Idaho, it is legal for one party to record another without notice. This means that, at any time, a client may have cameras in their home and is under no legal obligation to inform either you or GIST Cleaning management. This means that appropriate conduct is ***paramount***, whether or not a client is present.

### Appearance

Though cleaning is dirty work, it is also important that we present ourselves with appropriate cleanliness and professionality. This includes:

* Clean, practical clothing suitable for physical work  
* Good personal hygiene  
* Clothing should be respectful and appropriate for entering private home

---

## **7\. Employee Safety, Wellness & Physical Expectations**

### Physical Expectations

Residential cleaning is physically demanding work. Tasks may include bending, kneeling, lifting, standing for extended periods, scrubbing, and using cleaning products. Employees are expected to be able to perform these tasks with minimal difficulty and no anticipated damage to their body.

### Safety Expectations

* Follow all safety and training instructions on all labels, documents and instructional manuals  
* Use gloves or protective equipment when required or advisable  
* Never mix cleaning chemicals  
* Report injuries, accidents, or unsafe conditions immediately

Please inform us if you have any allergies or sensitivities to certain cleaning chemicals, and we will do our best to accommodate you. 

Your safety matters to us. Please speak up if something feels unsafe.

### Wellness

Employee wellness is a top priority for GIST Cleaning, and maintaining a good work-life balance is highly encouraged. If you find yourself ill or unwell and needing to rest and recover, please consider doing so and rescheduling with your client(s) if possible.

Client wellness is also a top priority. We do serve elderly clients, immunocompromised clients, and/or clients with small children. If you are running a fever and/or are confirmed with a contagious illness (e.g. COVID, influenza, norovirus), it is your responsibility to inform both your GIST Cleaning manager and your client(s)  each day you continue to run a fever and/or remain contagious. 

We always prefer to keep contagious illnesses at home, but understand that some employees may be reluctant to lose out on hours. If you wish to work while contagiously ill, you must receive consent from your client(s) for the day before performing your cleaning duties at their home *and* mask for the duration of your shift(s).

---

## **8\. Client Communication**

You will be largely responsible for communicating with your assigned clients regarding their services, as well as check-ins with management. The following is a quick-glance reference at what is included in your communication responsibilities as a **Residential Cleaning Technician**, and what is not. 

### Employee Responsibilities

* Communicating in person with clients regarding cleaning tasks or other job-related matters as needed  
* Messaging clients if you are running late, or need to cancel/reschedule  
* Coordinating any needed scheduling changes with clients  
  * Please inform your GIST Cleaning manager of any scheduling changes as soon as possible following the change.  
* Coordinating time slots with new clients who are assigned to you after their initial intake, according to availability

### Employer Responsibilities 

* Coordinating new client intakes  
* Assigning new clients to employees for scheduling   
* Addressing client complaints, accidents, or other liability issues

---

## **9\. Inclusivity & Understanding Policy**

From our website: 

“*One of GIST's core functional principles is **individual needs.***

*The key word in that sentence is **individual.***  
*​*  
*GIST is queer-friendly, disability-friendly, and mental health-inclusive.*

*GIST is also a no-shame space. We understand that we all have unique circumstances, both external and internal, that affect how we handle our spaces - and the depth or nature of the help we may need to handle them like we want to.*”

Operating by this policy is a cornerstone of our company culture, and is part of why our clients trust us. By signing this document, you are agreeing to operate according to these principles as a member of the GIST Cleaning team. 

---

## **10\. Anti-Discrimination & Harassment Policy**

GIST Cleaning is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment.

Discrimination or harassment based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, or any other protected status will not be tolerated by or from any GIST Cleaning employee, client, or person present in the client’s home while an employee is on shift.

Concerns should be reported to management promptly and will be taken seriously.

---

## **12\. Discipline & Termination**

We aim to address issues with communication and fairness. Depending on the situation, discipline may include verbal warnings, written warnings, or termination.

Because employment is at-will, termination may occur at any time, with or without cause, as allowed by law.

---

## **13\. Questions & Communication**

We encourage open communication. If you have questions about expectations, scheduling, safety, or anything else, please ask.

We believe the best work happens when people feel informed, respected, and supported.

---

## **14\. Acknowledgment**

This handbook may be updated as needed. Employees will be notified of significant changes.

# **EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT**

**Residential Cleaning Technician (Substitute)**

This Employment Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into as of the agreed-upon start date of **\[DATE\]**, by and between **GIST Cleaning,** a division of Sipes Enterprises, LLC (hereafter referred to as “Employer”) and \[EMPLOYEE NAME\] (hereafter referred to as “Employee”).

### **Note:** Substitute Position

Being a substitute is a vitally important position within our company, and a unique one. As such, there may be differences in how this document will pertain to the Employee. Laid out section by section, these differences are outlined below; please keep them in mind when reading through the Employment Agreement. 

#### All Sections

Depending on the conditions and expectations of the Employee’s position, discussed and agreed upon with the Employer upon hiring, the Employee’s agreed-upon position may contain the opportunity to build regular/recurring  hours with clientele. If this is the case, then some of these exceptions may no longer apply once the Employee has reached a certain threshold of hours per pay period.

#### Section 3: Work Schedule & Hours

* The Employee is expected to be available as needed to cover scheduled hours for other employees during extenuating circumstances.  
* Any arrangements regarding regular/recurring hours will be discussed with the Employer, and will otherwise follow the guidelines in this section as written.

#### Section 4: Compensation

* All listed timeframes (e.g. probationary period, performance review periods) begin upon the Employee’s first worked shift, not the date of hire. 

#### Section 6: Supplies, Equipment & Expenses

* The Employee’s cleaning kit will still be provided by the Employer; however, the listed supply allowance will be half the amount specified in this section, unless/until the Employee surpasses an hourly threshold of **20 hours per pay period.**   
* The Employee’s gas compensation card will be issued in the amount of **\$25** until they have surpassed an hourly threshold of **20 hours per pay period.**

---

## **1\. Employment Relationship**

The Employer hires the Employee as a **W-2 employee**, not as an independent contractor. Pursuant to Idaho law, as a “right-to-work” state, employment is **at-will**, meaning either the Employer or the Employee may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice. Nothing in this Agreement creates a contract for a specific length of time or guarantees continued employment. 

All work is performed in the State of Idaho, and employment is governed by Idaho and applicable federal law.

---

## **2\. Position & Job Duties**

The Employee is hired in the position of **Residential Cleaning Technician**.

The Employee’s primary duties include, but are not limited to:

* Standard residential cleaning tasks such as vacuuming, dusting, sweeping, mopping, bathroom and kitchen cleaning, trash removal, and light organizing.  
* Occasional **deep-cleaning tasks at client request**, including but not limited to:  
  * Cleaning inside refrigerators or ovens  
  * Cleaning underneath appliances or furniture  
  * Grout and tile detailing  
  * Baseboard cleaning  
  * Detailed bathroom or kitchen scrubbing

*For detailed information regarding job duties, please refer to your Employee Handbook, section 2\.*

These tasks may require physical activity such as bending, kneeling, lifting, standing for extended periods, and working with cleaning products.

All work is performed in **private residential homes**, and professionalism, respect, and discretion are required at all times.

---

## **3\. Work Schedule & Hours**

The Employee is expected to work approximately **20–25 hours per week**. Work hours may vary based on client demand, scheduling needs, and business conditions.

Additional hours, including the opportunity to move toward **full-time employment**, may be offered by mutual agreement but are not guaranteed.

The Employee agrees to arrive on time to scheduled cleanings and to notify the Employer and any scheduled clients as soon as possible if they are unable to work a scheduled shift.

*For more detailed information regarding scheduling and timeliness, please consult your Employee Handbook, section 4\.*

---

## **4\. Compensation**

The Employee will be paid **\$18.00 per hour**, paid on a **bimonthly** basis through payroll. There is a probationary period and structured opportunities for raises, as outlined below:

* The first **three (3) weeks** of employment are considered a probationary period. If performance or compatibility with the company’s standards are deemed substantially insufficient at the end of this period, or if the Employee violates company policies, the Employer may decide to terminate the Employee.  
* At the end of **six (6) months**, the Employee is eligible for a performance-based raise of **up to \$1.00 per hour**, at the Employer’s discretion.  
* After the initial review, performance reviews may occur every **six (6) months**, with the potential for raises of up to **\$0.25 per hour** per review.

All raises are **discretionary**, based on performance, reliability, client feedback, and business needs, and are not guaranteed.

Overtime will be paid at **one and one-half (1.5) times** the Employee’s regular hourly rate for all hours worked over **40 hours in a workweek**, in accordance with federal and Idaho law.

Paid time off is accrued at a rate of **1 hour per 25 hours worked**. *For more detailed information on acceptable use of PTO, please refer to your Employee Handbook, section 5\.*

---

## **5\. Timekeeping & Payroll Practices**

The Employee must accurately record all hours worked in a timely fashion using the timekeeping system provided and outlined by the Employer. Working “off the clock” is not permitted. Transportation time to and from client’s homes is not included in paid hours.

Falsifying time records, failing to accurately report hours worked, or chronic failure to record hours in a timely fashion may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

*For more detailed information on timekeeping practices and policies, please refer to your Employee Handbook, section 5\.*

---

## **6\. Supplies, Equipment & Expenses**

The Employee is responsible for:

* Reliable transportation to and from job sites  
* Appropriate work clothing and non-slip footwear  
* A personal phone for scheduling and communication purposes

The Employer will provide the Employee’s initial stock of cleaning supplies, tools, and equipment necessary to perform assigned duties upon their first day of work. 

Thereafter, the Employer will provide the Employee with a debit card, connected to an account held by Sipes Enterprises, LLC, to be used by the Employee ***exclusively*** for the purpose of purchasing supplies as needed. **\$75 per pay period** will be debited to this account for this purpose. ***This account is only to be used for supply purchases related to job duties,*** and receipts must be provided to the Employer on a regular basis. *For more detailed information on this policy, please refer to your Employee Handbook, section 3\.*

Employee’s transportation costs will be supplemented by the Employer in the amount of **\$50 per pay period**. This will be provided in the form of a prepaid Visa gift card. *For more detailed information on this policy, please refer to your Employee Handbook, section 3\.* 

The Employee is responsible for basic maintenance of provided equipment as necessary, or as outlined by the equipment’s instructional manual. 

The Employer will replace necessary  appliances and hardware (e.g. vacuum, mop, steam cleaner) as needed on a reasonable basis. Excessive breakage of appliances or hardware due to misuse or neglect may be investigated and charged to the Employee. 

Any purchases or reimbursements outside of already provided supplies, or excess to funds provided on the company debit card as outlined above, must be discussed & approved by the Employer in advance.

---

## **7\. Safety & Training**

The Employer will provide basic training as needed related to individual client needs and preferences, cleaning procedures, chemical safety, and safe work practices.

The Employee agrees to:

* Follow all procedural and safety instructions  
* Use personal protective equipment when necessary  
* Never mix cleaning chemicals  
* Report any injuries, accidents, or unsafe conditions immediately

Failure to follow safety procedures, or neglect of client needs and preferences, may result in disciplinary action.

---

## **8\. Confidentiality & Client Privacy**

The Employee will have access to private homes and personal client information. The Employee agrees to maintain strict confidentiality and client safety protocols, including but not limited to:

* Not sharing client names, addresses, schedules, or personal information   
  * Exceptions are limited to the Employer, or other Employees as necessary for shift coverage and agreed upon by the Employer  
* Not discussing or disclosing what is seen inside client homes  
  * Exceptions are limited to:  
    * Evidence of illegal activity that imminently or potentially endangers the Employee and/or residents of the home; or  
    * Occurrences that make the Employee feel unsafe while working in a client’s home  
  * If either of these Exceptions occur, the Employee is to reach out to the Employer directly and immediately, and allow the Employer to act upon the information provided at their discretion.  
* Not taking photos or videos inside client homes  
  * Exceptions are limited to:  
    * Photos taken with express, signed client consent and approval by the Employer, to be used for promotional materials; or  
    * Photos taken for liability purposes, such as an accident involving employee injury or damaged property  
* Not using client property, devices, or internet without permission  
* Maintaining the location, security, and confidentiality of all client keys and access codes at all times.

This obligation continues **during and after employment**.

---

## **9\. Non-Solicitation of Clients**

During employment and for **12 months after termination**, the Employee agrees not to solicit or accept cleaning work directly from any current or former GIST Cleaning clients they were introduced to through their employment.

This clause does **not** prohibit the Employee from working other jobs in the cleaning industry at their discretion if desired.

---

## **10\. Standards of Conduct**

The Employee agrees to maintain professional behavior at all times, including:

* No theft, dishonesty, or misuse of client or company property  
* No use of drugs or alcohol during work hours, or intoxication while on shift  
* Respectful communication with clients and coworkers  
* Following company policies and instructions

*For more detailed information regarding acceptable and unacceptable conduct, please refer to your Employer Handbook, section 6\.*

Violations may result in disciplinary action or immediate termination.

---

## **11\. Substance Use Policy**

The Employer reserves the right to drug test the Employee if it is deemed necessary by GIST management in response to client complaints, suspicious activity, or problematic behavior that may indicate potential substance usage and/or intoxication while on shift. The Employee reserves the right to refuse said drug testing, with the understanding that doing say may result in immediate termination of employment.

If the Employee is found by an administered drug test to be using illicit or intoxicating substances, and there is reasonable suspicion of the Employee being intoxicated while on shift, the Employee may be immediately terminated.

*For more detailed information regarding substance use, please refer to your Employee Handbook, section 6\.*

---

## **12\. Background Check**

As a condition of employment, the Employee consents to a background check. Costs for said background check will be covered by the Employer. 

---

## **13\. Termination of Employment**

Because employment is at-will, either party may terminate employment at any time.

If the Employee plans to terminate their employment, a minimum of two weeks’ notice is requested by the Employer for purposes of hiring a replacement. A minimum of four weeks is preferable for purposes of ensuring proper training for said replacement. 

***If a minimum of two weeks’ notice is given,*** any unused PTO balance will be added to the Employee’s final paycheck. ***The employee must attend their shifts from the time of notice*** until the time of their termination as a condition of claiming unused PTO. Immediate termination by the Employer may occur for serious misconduct, including but not limited to:

The Employee agrees to read the Employee Handbook in its entirety for a thorough understanding of company policies and procedures. The Employee also agrees to sign the Employee Handbook, stating that they understand and agree to the policies and procedures stated therein, as part of the Employment Agreement. For legal purposes, the Employee Handbook is considered an addendum to this contract.

## **15\. Compliance With Law**

Both the Employer and Employee agree to comply with all applicable **federal, Idaho state, and local employment laws**, including wage and hour laws, workplace safety requirements, and anti-discrimination laws.

# STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES -

## **General** (Residential Cleaning Technician)

***These are standard operating procedures and guidelines for GIST Cleaning employees in the Residential Cleaning Technician position to follow throughout all homes.** If you have any questions, or have any accommodation requests that cause conflict with one of the procedures outlined herein, please reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager.*

### **Client Homes**

#### Security Procedures

Each home will have its own security procedures; please refer to the individual SOP for the household you are cleaning, and reach out to your client directly if you have any questions.

#### Use of Client Resources

Reasonable use of the following client resources is permitted:

* Restroom facilities as needed  
* Seats or tables, as needed for breaks (see *Breaks*, below.)  
* Microwave, if needed for lunches and if wiped out afterward (please avoid microwaving seafood or other particularly pungent foods)  
* Water for drinking, from faucets or fridge dispenser if applicable  
* Electrical outlets for charging small personal devices  
* Paper towels or toilet paper for cleaning purposes  
* Wi-Fi (see *Wi-Fi,* below)

#### Wi-Fi

Some homes have WiFi available for use. For security purposes, this information is not included in any SOP’s; if you would like to utilize a client’s Wi-Fi, please reach out to them directly to request access.

### **Breaks**

GIST Cleaning has no official break policy, given that work hours are not continuous/consecutive. Please take meal breaks as-needed; you may do so between clients, or order a lunch to your location/bring a lunch with you. Please limit lunch breaks to 30 min at maximum. You may also take short sitting breaks as-needed to accommodate bodily strain. Smoking breaks are allowed only off-shift and off-site (see your *Employee Handbook,* section 6.) Excessive breaks, such that it is interfering with the ability to perform tasks thoroughly or in a timely fashion, may be cause for corrective action.

### **Supplies**

**RECOMMENDED SUPPLIES LIST**  
Your GIST Cleaning manager should provide you with your initial cleaning kit. As you work through the supplies provided and begin to replace what you have used/purchase further supplies with the company card provided, we recommend keeping the following supplies on hand. Some are required, and can/will be provided for your starting cleaning kit, and some are not required but are recommended to have if needed.   
**REQUIRED:**

* Vacuum  
* Damp mop  
* Rags  
* All-purpose and/or sanitizing surface cleaner  
* Toilet bowl cleaner  
* Sanitizing wipes (for toilets & surrounding areas *only*)  
* Glass cleaner  
* Bona or Murphy’s floor detergent (for wood floors)  
* Swiffer dusters, or non-brand equivalent  
* PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) as appropriate; gloves, face mask, protective glasses or goggles, etc.

**RECOMMENDED**:

* Grit cloth or Pumie pumice stones (for toilet rings & mineral staining)  
* Comet, or other mild abrasive cleaner  
* Swiffer mop & pads (good for tile floors or areas with high or visible hair content)  
* Furniture polish (we recommend Old English or Orange-Glo for wood furniture)  
* Stainless steel polish   
* Bristled scrubbing brushes (for cracks & crevices, textured surfaces, grout)  
* Razor and/or scraper  
* Paper towels

If any of these supplies were not provided in your starting kit and you would like to use them, you may purchase them at your liberty with your company supplies account - or, if additional desired supplies represent a cost that will infringe on your ability to replace necessities, reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager to discuss reimbursement or having the company purchase it for you.

***Follow any and all instructions listed on any and all cleaning supplies.** This includes usage instructions and guidelines, dilution instructions, maintenance protocols, and safety requirements, **including any recommended PPE.** Failure to do so will result in corrective action or, in extreme cases, immediate termination.*

 ***If you have any doubts or unanswered questions** regarding supply use, please use an appropriate internet search engine to find answers - or, if needed, reach out to your GIST Cleaning manager.*   
   
**Spray Bottles**

* Re-use spray bottles. Wherever possible or applicable, we heavily prefer purchasing concentrated solutions and refilling bottles as we go. This reduces waste, and is more cost effective when purchasing cleaners. **Follow all dilution instructions and mixing precautions.**

**Brushes, Sponges and Pads**

* Utilize only **non-scratch** abrasive pads & sponges. These are typically colored blue across most major brands, but always check to be sure.  
* **Rinse brushes** after use, to prevent caking and/or carrying residue or bacteria between locations.  
* Replace any brushes, sponges or pads as needed once they begin to lose abrasion or show signs of wear and tear that affects their usefulness.

**Razors & Scrapers**

* **Always follow safety precautions when using bladed implements.**  
* **Carefully** wipe the blade clean/dry before retracting and replacing in your kit to prevent rusting or dulling  
* Replace any blades that have become dull, rusty, or bent. 

**All Purpose Cleaner**

* Ensure you are following all dilution and mixing instructions where applicable.   
* Best used for surfaces not requiring full sanitization. (Examples: kitchen counters, microwaves, living space surfaces, sinks

**Sanitizing/Disinfectant Cleaner**

* Ensure you are following all dilution and mixing instructions where applicable.  
* **If using bleach**-containing disinfectant cleaners, take extra care not to mix with any other chemicals as bleach can be volatile. **Take care/do not use around non-colorsafe fabrics.**  
* Best used for hard surfaces in high-microbe traffic areas, such as bathrooms and kitchen sinks.   
* Can be used on almost any hard surface if preferred, but can be more caustic than some all-purpose cleaners; follow product precautions and use best judgment. 

**Toilet Bowl Cleaner**

* **If using bleach**-containing toilet bowl cleaners, take extra care not to mix with any other chemicals as bleach can be volatile.   
* After scrubbing, flush multiple times until all residue is gone, including from under bowl. Residue left unrinsed and/or unflushed can erode ceramic, or make pets sick. 

**Sanitizing Wipes**

* **We highly prefer to use sanitizing wipes for toilets** rather than rags and spray cleaners; no lint or fabric residue is left behind, and it reduces chances of carrying harmful bacteria to other areas.  
* To reduce waste, **use only for toilets** and surrounding floor areas, or anywhere else that may have come into contact with human or animal waste. 

**Murphy’s Detergent**

* Murphy’s Detergent is a concentrate. Ensure you are following all dilution and mixing instructions.   
* Mix an appropriate amount of Murphy’s and warm water into a spray bottle according to dilution instructions, and spray on well-finished wood floors before damp-mopping with an appropriate damp-fabric mop. 

**Furniture Polish**

* Use according to product instructions.   
* If using Old English or Orange-Glo (which we recommend for any household with older wooden furniture), use only on items that are plain finished wood. Do not use on items that are painted wood, or coated/composite wood.

**Stainless Steel Polish**

* Use according to product instructions.  
* We recommend using a microfiber towel for stainless steel polishing. 

**Comet**

* Comet is the most price-effective and commonly used mild abrasive cleaner, and also contains bleach, so it serves multiple purposes and is our recommended powder cleanser.   
* Use for sinks, tubs, glass stovetops, and treated stainless steel faucets to cut through grease, grime, and everyday hard water buildup. You can also use to remove stains from some countertops.  
* Use according to product instructions.   
* **Do not overscrub** or apply excessive pressure, as it may result in scratching on some surfaces.   
* For a more abrasive cleaner for tougher jobs, we recommend **The Pink Stuff** paste.

**Swiffer Mop**

* Use according to product instructions.   
* Best used for tile or linoleum floors, or areas with excessive hair/other potential left-behind matter  
* Replace pads with appropriate frequency, and watch for streaking

### Surfaces

**General**

* Utilize **dry rags** with an appropriate cleaner or polish **on living space surfaces** as needed to remove fingerprints or smudging or polish/condition surfaces that require it. (Examples: entertainment centers, end tables, decorative surfaces, shelves) This helps to reduce the chances of moisture streaking/staining on surfaces that do not require water.  
* Utilize **wet rags** with an appropriate cleaner **on kitchen, bathroom and dining room** surfaces. **Water is essential** to catching sticky spots, spills, grease, and food residue with the most efficiency - reducing the “elbow grease” required and lessening the chances of missing individual spots - and gives you least chance of leaving undesirable bits of streaking or residue behind. **Wet your rag thoroughly, wring damp,** and then **rinse as needed** as you go to remove crumbs, grease or residue.   
* Utilize **non-scratch abrasive pads** (typically blue) for the initial scrub of sinks & faucets, following up with a rag for the rinse & dry; and as needed for everyday mineral buildup, stuck food, etc. **Exercise best judgment**; if you’re not sure whether a surface will be damaged by an abrasive pad, forego utilizing one until you’ve done some research. A quick Google search will usually tell you what you need to know\!

**Stainless Steel**

* **For steel sinks and faucets:** use an appropriate cleaner and rag/pad for the level of grease, grime, or hard water buildup in/on the sink. Wet wipe or rinse after initial scrub, then wipe dry. Polish if needed/desired once surface is dry (stainless steel polish combined with extra moisture tends to leave residue.) **If using abrasive cleaner**, do not over-scrub or apply excessive pressure.   
* **For appliances:** use an appropriate cleaner and rag/pad to clean off any grease, grime or residue. Polish once surface is dry.

**Wood Floors**

* **Do not wet/sponge mop\!** It will damage and warp wood flooring. Damp mopping (Swiffer, Bona or other fabric pad mop) is okay, so long as appropriate detergent is used and moisture level does not leave trails or puddles.   
* **Only** use floor cleaners that are explicitly labelled as being safe for wood floors.  
* **If you notice warping or damaged finish** when you first begin cleaning a client’s house, please take pictures and ensure the client is aware so any potential liability for damage can be mitigated.

**Wood Furniture**

* **Only** use moistened rags if finish is fully intact. Otherwise, utilize dry rags.  
* **Only** use wood-safe cleaners.   
* Utilize oil-based wood polish regularly to keep wood lustrous and maintain older wood.

**Painted Walls/Cabinets/Baseboards**

* **Do not use** abrasive pads, as it will wear away most paint.  

### Appliances

**Vacuum**

* Follow manufacturer instructions for regular maintenance, including  
  * Emptying dust cup when full  
  * Blowing/beating out and regularly washing dust and air filters  
  * Periodically removing wound-up hair, string or other materials from brush roll  
* Utilize appropriate vacuum settings for the floor you are cleaning  
* Utilize attachments as necessary for baseboards, corners, upholstery, vents, etc.  
* **If using a client vacuum**, always exercise caution and care.  
* Report any issues or breakages to your GIST Cleaning manager immediately. 

**Mop**

* Thoroughly rinse/wring mop after use to avoid mildewy odors  
* Thoroughly hot-rinse fabric pads for damp mops in between households, and wash regularly with laundry.   
* Report any issues or breakages to your GIST Cleaning manager. 

**Steam Cleaner or Other Misc Hardware**

* Follow manufacturer instructions for use and maintenance.  
* Take care using a steam cleaner on painted surfaces, and avoid using on wood.  
* Report any issues or breakages to your GIST Cleaning manager.
